title: Slab-built shield wall hanging
subtitle: An air-dry clay shield shape with relief decoration, ready to hang as wall art
excerpt: A simple shield silhouette cut from an air-dry clay slab gives a strong, graphic shape for wall decoration. The flat surface accepts stamp work, carved lines, or applied clay motifs. Hanging hardware is pressed in before drying. The whole piece can be completed in one session and hung after drying.
sourceNotes: Shield wall hanging in air-dry clay derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat, even sheet of clay rolled to a consistent thickness
The stage at which the shield holds its shape for decoration without distorting
Fully dried clay, ready for sealing and hanging

content.text: A shield shape is one of the most useful air-dry clay wall-hanging forms because the flat face takes decoration well and the pointed base adds visual weight without extra material. The
slab
approach , roll, cut, decorate, hang , keeps the process simple. The result can be a subtle wall accent or a bold focal point depending on how it is finished.
Cut the shield shape

Draw a shield template on card: a rectangle 120 mm wide by 100 mm tall, then a triangle beneath it 120 mm wide and 60 mm tall. The rectangle forms the upper flat section; the triangle gives the pointed lower portion.
Roll the clay to 8 mm thickness. Place the card template on the slab and cut around it with the fettling knife held vertically.
Round the two upper corners of the shield slightly with a damp finger , sharp corners tend to chip after drying.
Press in the hanging hardware

While the clay is still soft, press a D-ring hook into the reverse side of the shield, centred at the top, 15 mm from the upper edge. Press the hook base firmly into the clay and smear clay over the base plate to lock it in place.
Decorate the front face
At
leather-hard

stage, stamp or incise a pattern on the front face. Options include a central geometric motif stamped with a pottery stamp, diagonal incised lines carved with a needle tool, or a simple leaf or star motif built up from thin ropes of clay attached with slip.
If attaching clay ropes or applied motifs, score and slip both surfaces before pressing together. Blend the join with a damp finger.
Dry, finish, and hang
Dry the shield on a flat surface. Check periodically that the shield stays flat , if it begins to curl, flip it face-down and allow to finish drying upside-down.
At
bone-dry
stage, paint with two coats of acrylic or coloured slip. A dark base colour with a dry-brushed lighter highlight over the raised decoration looks effective.
Seal with two coats of PVA varnish. Allow to dry fully before hanging.

items.solution: Flip face-down at leather-hard stage to correct any early curl. If bone-dry and still warped, it cannot be straightened. For future pieces, keep the thickness consistent and dry on a porous surface.

items.problem: Applied decoration falls off after drying
items.solution: Applied elements need score-and-slip joins on both surfaces. If an element has come off, reattach with PVA adhesive at bone-dry stage.
